fraction.title: Fraction
fraction.intro: A fraction represents a part of a whole. It consists of two parts:
fraction.numerator: Numerator: The top number, representing how many parts we have
fraction.denominator: Denominator: The bottom number, representing how many equal parts the whole is divided into
fraction.readExample1: is read as "three-fourths" or "three over four"
fraction.readExample3: is read as "five-eighths" or "five over eight"
fraction.pizzaExample: If you cut a pizza into 8 equal slices and eat 3 slices, you ate {fraction} of the pizza.

types.title: Types of Fractions
types.mixedNumber: Mixed Number: A whole number plus a proper fraction

equivalent.title: Equivalent Fractions
equivalent.intro: Equivalent fractions are fractions that represent the same value, even though they have different numerators and denominators.
equivalent.multiply: Multiply both numerator and denominator by the same number
equivalent.divide: Or divide both by the same number (simplifying)

pizzaTrick.title: 🍕 Pizza Slice Trick
pizzaTrick.content: Think of fractions as pizza slices! The denominator is how many slices the pizza is cut into, and the numerator is how many slices you have. So {fraction} means "3 slices out of a pizza cut into 4 equal pieces."

simplification.title: ✂️ Quick Simplification Trick
simplification.intro: To simplify fractions quickly, check if both numbers are even. If yes, divide by 2. Repeat until you can't anymore:
simplification.proTip: Pro tip: If both end in 0 or 5, try dividing by 5!

conversion.title: 🔄 Two-Way Conversion Trick
conversion.improperInstructions: Divide numerator by denominator. Whole = quotient, Fraction = remainder/denominator
conversion.mixedInstructions: Multiply whole × denominator, add numerator, keep denominator

lcm.step1: LCM(3, 5) = 15 (since 3 and 5 share no common factors)

gcf.title: 🎲 Quick GCF (Greatest Common Factor) Trick
gcf.intro: To find GCF of two numbers, use the "division ladder" method:
gcf.euclid: Or use Euclid's algorithm: Divide larger by smaller, replace larger with remainder, repeat until remainder is 0.

keyConcept.title: Understanding Denominators
keyConcept.content: The denominator tells us how many equal parts make up one whole. A larger denominator means each part is smaller.

shadedArea.question: Which fraction represents the shaded area?
shadedArea.description: Imagine a circle divided into 4 equal parts, with 3 parts shaded.
shadedArea.explanation: Correct! Since 3 out of 4 equal parts are shaded, the fraction is {fraction}.
shadedArea.remember: Remember: numerator (3) = parts shaded, denominator (4) = total parts.
shadedArea.hint: Count how many parts are shaded (numerator) and how many total parts there are (denominator).

simplify.hint: Find the greatest common factor (GCF) of 24 and 36, then divide both by it.

convert.instruction: Enter your answer as a decimal. For example, 2¾ = 2.75
convert.hint: Divide 17 by 5. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder over 5 is the fraction.

improperToMixed.problem: Convert the improper fraction {fraction} to a mixed number.
improperToMixed.hint: Try dividing 11 by 4. How many times does 4 go into 11? What is left over?
improperToMixed.step1Title: Divide the numerator by the denominator
improperToMixed.step2Title: The quotient becomes the whole number
improperToMixed.step3Title: The remainder becomes the new numerator

theorem.title: Equivalent Fractions Test
theorem.statement: Two fractions are equivalent if and only if their cross products are equal.

conclusion.title: Congratulations!
conclusion.message: You've learned the basics of fractions, including proper/improper fractions, mixed numbers, and equivalent fractions. These concepts are fundamental for adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing fractions in future lessons.
